No Flood Watch is active for northern Arizona today, but this trail crosses Fossil Creek in a canyon, so avoid hiking during and shortly after any storm. Hike early morning and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: The Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026: South Kaibab Trail is now open only from the trailhead to Tip-Off Point (about 4.4 miles down) and closed below that due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding, a more restrictive cutoff than the prior Black Bridge closure point (Source: National Park Service, Key Hiking Messages, updated September 3, 2026). Ooh Aah Point (0.9 miles) and Cedar Ridge (1.5 miles), the trail's popular shorter destinations, remain within the open section. This follows a severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that destroyed nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. Additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, or rockfall, so conditions could change quickly. This trail is fully sun exposed with no water source below the trailhead; confirm current water status at the trailhead before descending. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: The Park Service expanded closures on September 3, 2026: Bright Angel Trail is now open only from the trailhead to Havasupai Gardens (formerly Indian Garden) at the Tonto Trail intersection, a shorter cutoff than the prior River Resthouse closure point; the trail is closed below that intersection except for river-trip exchanges at Pipe Creek Beach (Source: National Park Service, Key Hiking Messages, updated September 3, 2026). Havasupai Gardens itself remains accessible via the open section of trail, with water available there. This follows a severe flash flood in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29 that closed Phantom Ranch, the North Kaibab Trail, and the river-crossing bridges; the park states there is no estimated reopening at this time. Grand Canyon National Park separately advises day hikers descend no farther than 1.5 miles from the upper trailhead due to elevated Inner Canyon heat risk regardless of warning status. Water status can change suddenly, so verify current conditions before descending. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

rim-trail.note: No closures reported today; the Rim Trail is not affected by the Bright Angel Canyon flash flood closure, confirmed unchanged today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch (including Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins), and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, confirmed today against the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page, updated September 3, 2026 as part of an expanded closure list issued that day. A severe flash flood struck Bright Angel Canyon around 2:30pm on August 29, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and requiring an aerial evacuation of 62 people from the Phantom Ranch and lower North Kaibab area; no injuries were reported. Colorado River traffic through the area, including rafting, remains halted. The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall with little to no warning even when storms are not visible overhead, especially given ongoing Dragon Bravo Fire burn scar hazards. Water status at the North Kaibab Trailhead, Supai Tunnel, and Cottonwood Campground should be considered uncertain until the park posts a post-flood update. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
